subject.title: /learn's skill-authoring-and-apply pipeline has no owner gate, unlike the equivalent plugin-install path

question: Where should OpenClaw enforce owner-tier authorization for Skill Workshop lifecycle writes created or approved from chat?
rationale: The source-reproducible bypass is clear, but the durable security boundary spans `/learn`, dynamic tool execution, service-level apply/reject/quarantine, `/approve`, and gateway-admin exceptions.

options.title: Gate all mutation boundaries
options.body: Require owner-tier or explicit admin authority at `/learn`, lifecycle tool/service execution, and plugin approval resolution for Skill Workshop lifecycle writes.

options.title: Gate chat entry points only
options.body: Block non-owner `/learn` and `/approve` while leaving lower-level tool/service execution governed by current approval policy, which is smaller but easier to bypass through other surfaces.

options.title: Fold into broader approval design
options.body: Handle this under the broader Skill Workshop approval-evidence contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93278, accepting that this concrete bypass remains open until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Gate all mutation boundaries
recommendation.body: Require owner-tier or explicit admin authority at `/learn`, lifecycle tool/service execution, and plugin approval resolution for Skill Workshop lifecycle writes.

likelyOwner.reason: They opened the `/learn` feature request and have adjacent same-chat approval routing history, making them the best available owner for the boundary decision.
